name: Smartlead
tagline: Run small permission-based email sequences with reply and suppression handling

tiers.name: Base
tiers.limits: 2,000 contacts, 6,000 email sends/month, 2,000 verified emails, unlimited email accounts.
tiers.notes: All plans have free trial; no credit card required.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 30,000 contacts, 90,000 email sends/month, 30,000 verified emails, unlimited email accounts.

tiers.name: Unlimited Smart
tiers.limits: Unlimited contacts, 150,000 email sends/month, 50,000 verified emails, unlimited email accounts.

tiers.name: Unlimited Prime
tiers.limits: Unlimited contacts, 500,000 email sends/month, 170,000 verified emails, 3 SmartServers + OAuth, 3+ clients/workspaces included.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; free trial with no credit card, but no ongoing free caps published.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Whitelabeling add-on $29/mo per client workspace; SmartServer $39/server/month; SmartSenders domains/mailboxes add cost; verification credits one-time or monthly; SmartDelivery and SmartDialer are separate products.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Smartlead, run small permission-based email sequences with reply and suppression handling. The hard boundary is multi-inbox scale, warm-up, deliverability infrastructure, routing, and agency features, plus proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects.
coreLoopDIY: Import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest email sequence, enforce sending limits and suppression handling, and track replies without supplying proprietary contact data.
whatYouLose: multi-inbox scale, warm-up, deliverability infrastructure, routing, and agency features
moatNotes: proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects
ongoingBurden: consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Smartlead because the durable value is accurate contact data and deliverability infrastructure; a sequence editor alone is not the product. The recurring cost buys consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Mautic
priorArt.desc: Open-source marketing automation platform with campaigns, contacts, and email workflows.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: A campaign engine with reply, bounce and unsubscribe handling; mailbox rotation and warm-up are deliberately absent.

rejectedAlternatives.name: listmonk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A fine newsletter sender, but it does not watch replies and stop a sales sequence; wrong kind of email automation.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a small permission-based outreach console DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Smartlead in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and a user-chosen transactional email provider; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest email sequence, enforce sending limits and suppression handling, and track replies without supplying proprietary contact data.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Accept CSV imports only after the user confirms lawful collection and records the source.
Provide contact fields, tags, suppression status, consent notes, and a complete change history.
Build a short email sequence with delays, business-hour windows, and per-domain rate limits.
Use the configured provider for sends and process delivery, bounce, complaint, and unsubscribe webhooks.
Stop sequences immediately on reply, bounce, complaint, suppression, or manual pause.
Show deliverability warnings, daily send totals, and a mandatory preview before activation.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out scraping protected platforms.
Deliberately leave out buying or generating personal contact data.
Deliberately leave out automated inbox warm-up networks and evasion of provider limits.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
